subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Calculate the spin only magnetic moment of the Fe²⁺(aq) ion.

verification.note: Unit 11 (d and f Block Elements) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 8 ("8. d & f BLOCK ELEMENTS"), book pp.91-94, which prints this question on book p.91 as VSAQ 4. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. ARITHMETIC CHECKED: Fe (Z = 26) is [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²; Fe²⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s⁰; six electrons in five d orbitals give one pair and four singles, so n = 4; μ = √(4 × 6) = √24 = 4.899 BM, written 4.90 BM. The book prints 4.9 BM, the same number. NOTE ON THE MODEL: the formula is spin-only and drops the orbital contribution, which for high-spin Fe²⁺(aq) is not negligible — measured values run above 5 BM. That limit is stated on the card so the student does not read 4.90 BM as an experimental prediction.

steps.why: The 4s electrons leave first, so Fe²⁺ is 3d⁶ and not 3d⁴ 4s². Filling six electrons into five orbitals by Hund's rule gives one pair and four singles, so the unpaired count is four. Getting n right is the whole calculation; the formula then does the rest.
common_mistakes: Removing the 3d electrons first and writing Fe²⁺ as 3d⁴ 4s². The 4s electrons are removed first.
Counting six unpaired electrons in 3d⁶. There are only five orbitals, so the sixth electron pairs up and n = 4.
steps.memory_tip: 3d⁶ is one pair plus four singles: six electrons in five boxes leaves four alone.
steps.margin_note: Write the atom, then the ion, then n. The unpaired count is where this calculation is usually lost.

steps.label: Substitution and answer
lines: An unpaired electron makes the ion
This is a spin only value: it counts
electron spin and leaves out orbital
motion, so the measured value for
Fe²⁺(aq) is a little above 4.90 BM.
steps.why: √24 = 4.899, which is written 4.90 BM to three figures; the book prints 4.9 BM, the same number. The formula is called spin only because it drops the orbital contribution to the moment. For most first-series ions in water that contribution is small, but for high-spin Fe²⁺ it is not, so the measured moment comes out above the calculated one. Saying so is honest and costs one line.
common_mistakes: Using the number of d electrons in place of n. Here n is 4, not 6.
Leaving the answer as √24. Work the square root out and write 4.90 BM with the unit.
steps.memory_tip: n(n+2) with n = 4 gives 24, and √24 is just under 5.
steps.margin_note: Box the number with the unit BM. A bare 4.90 with no unit usually loses part of this mark.

insider_note: The formula and the final number are both easy marks; the part actually lost is the unpaired count. Show 3d⁶ as one pair and four singles before substituting.
